text: Casual is not on offer from your side of this. Your Pluto has fused with their Venus, the part of them that decides what is enjoyable, who is worth their regard, and how affection gets shown. Joined to your depth, none of that stays a light matter. They may notice that the ordinary setting they use with almost everyone has stopped working on you, and that whatever they feel about you arrives at full volume or not at all. What happens to their values in your company is real and mostly nobody's doing. Around you, what they enjoy gets weighed. A preference they held because holding it was easy begins to feel thin, and a pleasure they had been treating as a habit either turns serious or drops off the list. People often change what they wear, what they listen to, and what they will sit through inside a contact like this. Some of that is a gift. Some of it costs them a comfortable setting they had been using for years, and they may not thank you for it at the time. Their side of it is quieter and easy to overlook. Your Pluto marks ground that most company steps around. It gets handled carefully, or called a lot to deal with, or quietly avoided. Venus does none of that. Their instinct is to find things enjoyable, and aimed at your depth it does the one thing you probably do not expect: it likes you there. Being wanted at the exact place where you are used to being managed is not a small event, and it can unsettle you further than your intensity ever unsettles them. There is a real charge in this and it deserves plain statement rather than decoration. The two of you are likely to be more taken up with each other than the type or the length of the acquaintance would explain. That is the geometry, and geometry has nothing to say about how anybody behaves. Two people with this contact can rebuild what affection means to them from the ground up, or spend years measuring who is more invested, and no aspect picks between those. The pressure you feel is worth naming too. Pleasant treatment is hard for you to take at face value here, and you may keep hunting for the true version underneath a perfectly sincere kindness. That is a habit of yours rather than evidence about them. Their warmth may be exactly what it looks like. Where you grow is in tolerating enjoyment that has nothing underneath it. Your instinct is to find the root of a thing, and a Venus contact keeps handing you things with no root: an afternoon, a meal, a song they played twice. Letting one of those be what it is, without opening it, is difficult work for you, and it is exactly the work this contact sets.

Think of this one as a tool left in a drawer. Your Pluto and their Venus can reach each other without strain, and neither of you is under any obligation to pick the connection up. Weeks can pass in which the two of you are pleasant company and nothing more. When one of you does reach for it, the register changes inside a sentence. What you offer them, when the offer gets taken, is an honest read on what they care about. They bring you something they like: a plan, a purchase they are talking themselves into, a person they are extending the benefit of the doubt. You can see what it will actually cost them, and you can say so without heat and without needing to win. Most of the responses they get are flattery or argument. Yours is neither, which is why they come back to you with the questions where liking a thing and the thing being good have come apart. Their side of the trade is lighter, and you may need it more than they need yours. Venus makes company pleasant. Around them your depth is not a problem to be handled or an intensity to be admired. It is simply welcome, and the welcome costs nothing, so you can put something serious down in their presence without it becoming an occasion. If you are used to being the one who makes a room go quiet, that registers as an unfamiliar sort of rest. Put the two of you on a decision with money or standing in it and you cover different halves. They can tell what is worth having and what it will be like to live with. You can tell what holding on to it will demand, and who is going to be exposed if it goes wrong. Neither read is much use without the other. The limit is written into the angle. Sextiles insist on nothing. You can spend a decade near this person, aware in a vague way that they take you more easily than most people do, and never once take it past the surface, since no crisis will arrive to settle the matter for you. Left in the drawer, the tool stays a tool nobody used. A low-volume version of the intensity runs through it as well. Around them your appetites get more definite. Something you would once have called fine becomes something you want plainly, and something you had been enduring becomes something you decline. No scene is required for either. Growth here comes in small trades rather than in crises. Each time they hand you something they value and you tell them the truth about it, the exchange gets easier to make. Each time you let their company be enjoyable instead of significant, you get a little of your ordinary week back.

What you take seriously, they would rather enjoy, and the two positions meet at an awkward angle. Your Pluto squares their Venus, so the part of you that cannot leave a surface alone keeps arriving at the part of them that was trying to have a nice evening. You are not doing it to spoil anything. It is how you are built. Still, a person whose method is charm finds you hard to be light around, and you find their lightness hard to credit. The friction shows first in how the two of you handle an easy hour. They offer pleasantness, and pleasantness gets most people through. You want to know what it is covering, and a good deal of the time it is covering nothing at all. The habit of looking for the real version under a kind remark is yours, and here it lands on someone whose kind remarks are frequently just kind. That misreading costs you more than it costs them. Their side is not passive. What their Venus asks of you is that you enjoy something without opening it, and the request presses on the least developed part of your equipment. An afternoon with no subject underneath it is a real request, not an evasion. So is warmth handed over plainly and often, with nobody checking what it is made of. You are being asked to be easy, which is the one thing your depth is not, and almost nobody else in your life is pressing you on it with any conviction. The tradition writes this angle up in lurid terms, so a flat statement is worth making. The square puts force between what you intensify and what they find pleasant and fair. What it does not do is describe behavior. Two people at this angle can come out with a much clearer sense of what they each value, or can circle one standoff for years, and the chart decides neither. Hard angles produce movement, and the movement here runs through worth. In their company you find out what you would pay for, what you have been accepting because refusing looked ungrateful, and what your regard is actually worth when you give it. Praise stops landing on you unless it is exact. Your own regard comes out at a slower rate, and once it is out, nobody argues you back from it. You develop here by letting a pleasant thing stand. Not every smooth surface is a lid. If you can take their warmth at the value they offer it, and hold your own seriousness without needing them to match it, most of the heat becomes usable. The strain does not leave, and nothing about this angle mellows on its own. What changes is the use you both get from it: you learn to be enjoyed, they learn to be met, and both of those are harder than they sound.

Being serious costs you nothing here, which is rarer than it sounds. Your Pluto reaches their Venus along an easy angle, so the part of you that will not leave anything at the surface meets the part of them that decides what is enjoyable, and it meets no resistance. They are not braced for you. Your weight arrives as devotion rather than as pressure, and they take it that way without anybody having to explain the difference. The everyday version is that your attention is a pleasure to be on the receiving end of. When you notice something about them, they feel understood instead of examined. When you commit to something of theirs, they feel backed instead of owned. This is often the person who tells you that your seriousness is one of the better things about you, which is not the standard review. Your return is somewhere to put depth that does not turn heavy. Intensity kept indoors goes stale and starts working on its owner. Pointed at company you enjoy, the same capacity becomes generous: you defend their interests when they are not in the room, you remember what they care about in detail that surprises them, you spend on their behalf without bothering to explain why. The trouble with a comfortable angle is that it never asks to be used. This can sit as a good feeling for years without ever being said out loud, because no discomfort arrives to make either of you name what the connection is. Ease is not the same thing as depth reached. There is a second hazard, and it belongs to this pair rather than to trines in general. When your intensity is this comfortable to give, you can start assuming it is always welcome. It is not, and the people in your life who flinch at it are not failing you. Their Venus is unusually good at receiving what you carry. That is a fact about the fit, not a standard the rest of your company should be measured against. There is the matter of taste as well. Your appetites tend to get refined in this contact rather than sharpened. They make things nicer, and you find you enjoy being made comfortable, which for somebody with your equipment can feel faintly suspicious. It is allowed. Worked rather than admired, this holds up under conditions that flatten louder connections. You get to be entirely yourself here, including the parts other company handles at arm's length, and none of it costs the connection anything. What you take from it, whatever the two of you turn out to be to each other, is evidence that your depth can be a pleasure to somebody. That is not a thing you were ever likely to learn on your own.

They can make almost anything pleasant, and you cannot leave almost anything alone. Those two capacities sit directly across from each other here, so they do not blend and neither one gives way. Under most exchanges between you a quiet argument runs about what things are worth, and it is rarely stated in those words. What you meet in them is a person your seriousness does not reach by the usual route. Faced with your attention, most people either open up or get defensive. Venus does a third thing: it stays pleasant. They smooth the moment, offer the agreeable version, change the subject with real grace, and you are left holding a question with nowhere to put it. From where you stand that can look like evasion. From where they stand it is good manners, and they are not wrong either. You do something equally awkward to them. Around you the pleasant version stops working, first with you and then, inconveniently, elsewhere. You notice the calculation inside a kindness. You notice when a preference of theirs was inherited rather than chosen. Being read at that depth is uncomfortable for someone whose whole method is keeping things nice, and it is also more accurate than the treatment they get almost anywhere else. The pull is worth describing plainly. Oppositions hold. Attention runs heavier in both directions than the type or the length of the acquaintance would explain. Consumer astrology likes this pair as a cautionary tale. What is actually here is weight, and weight predicts nothing about how two people treat each other. A division of labor forms early in this and is worth catching while it is still reversible. It is convenient for the two of you to settle into the arrangement where you are the deep one and they are the light one, where you carry the truth and they carry the good manners. Each half turns out to live in both of you. The angle only stretches them to opposite ends of a single line, and while the roles are running, neither of you has to do the other's job. Oppositions complete as well as confront. Left alone, your intensity has nothing to spend itself on except old material. Left alone, their charm keeps a nice surface over a room nobody has entered in years. Facing each other, the two correct. You get taught that pleasure is not a distraction from serious life, and they get shown that being known is survivable. Two things tend to survive this contact whatever becomes of the connection: a working figure for what your regard is worth, and the discovery that being liked is not always a transaction.

Around you, their impulses stop being disposable. Your Pluto has joined their Mars, the part of them that wants, decides, and pushes, and a conjunction leaves no space between the two functions. An irritation they would have dropped anywhere else stays with them. A plan they mentioned in passing becomes something they are actually going to do. Neither of you switched that on. The contact removes the option of doing things by halves. What you add to the exchange is consequence. They arrive with appetite and speed. You supply the sense that the thing matters, that it goes somewhere, that it will still be true next year. People often work harder in your vicinity than they can account for afterwards. Some of the largest efforts of their life may happen inside the range of this connection, and the source of the fuel will be hard for them to locate. What comes back to you is motion, which you do not generate easily. Your material tends to sit. You can carry an intention for years without acting on it, because knowing a thing and moving on it are different muscles and yours are not equally developed. They act. In their company what you have been holding still starts to move, sometimes before you have finished deciding whether you wanted it to. Conflict here deserves plain description. Disagreements between you rarely stay the size of the subject that started them. Their end wants the matter settled today. Your end goes for the root and finds one. Once the two of you are down there, changing the topic ends nothing, because your side of this does not forget and does not tire. That is worth knowing about yourself rather than about them. A conjunction gives you no distance from which to check any of it. Wanting something near this person feels like the truth about what you want. Anger near them feels like evidence about who they are. A fair amount of both is the geometry at work, and telling the two apart is most of what this contact asks. Force is what the geometry supplies. The use is not in the chart. Pointed at a task the two of you chose, this pairing gets through work that most connections cannot begin. Left with nowhere to go, it takes the connection itself as the subject, which is the version that wears both people out. What develops in you here is a sense of timing. You are used to depth arriving slowly and being right when it does. Beside someone whose whole method is to move first and correct later, you find out how much of your certainty was thoroughness and how much of it was delay.

Nothing about this one announces itself, which is the first thing to know about it. Your Pluto and their Mars are within reach of each other, no more than that. Their drive is available to your depth, your depth is available to their drive, and if neither of you reaches, the acquaintance stays agreeable and nothing at all is lost. Taken up, it runs like this. They come to you with something they want and a plan already in motion. You can see where the weight actually sits, which is often not where they are pushing, and you say so in a sentence. They do not hear a brake. Mars at this angle takes it as better aim, changes line, and goes at the thing again with the same appetite. Being used that quickly is unusual for you, since depth of your sort more often gets treated as a mood to be waited out. What you get is an exit from your own patience. You can hold a read on a situation for years without acting, and the holding starts to feel like judgment long after it has become avoidance. They are not built that way. Near them, things you have been carrying get done this month. Some of it will be work you would have gone on postponing indefinitely, and you may be mildly annoyed at how simple it turns out to be. Arguments between you tend to be usable. You do not startle, and they have no need of the polite version, so a disagreement can reach the real subject on the first attempt instead of the fourth and not take the rest of the week down with it. This is a person you can be blunt with, which is a shorter list than most people assume. The angle offers and never insists. Ten years can pass in easy company with nothing ever put through this contact, because the lighter option is always at hand and nothing here objects. What is not used does not decay. It simply never happens. Building it is deliberate on both sides. Hand them the thing you have been circling for a year and let them start on it before you feel ready. Say the hard sentence early, since it will not cost you what it costs elsewhere. Over a long acquaintance this contact gives you something you are unlikely to arrange for yourself, which is a route out of your own depth and back into an ordinary week where things get finished.

They push. You do not move, and the not-moving is not a decision you take each time. Your Pluto squares their Mars, so their capacity to act meets your capacity to hold at right angles, and neither converts into the other. They want it settled this week. You run on a timescale where waiting is itself a position, and to them the wait starts to look like the answer. You rarely block them by argument. More often the ground under a step of theirs turns out to belong to you, or a matter they had filed as closed has another floor beneath it. Their usual methods stop working here, and the reflex when a method stops working is to apply it harder. That is where the heat comes from, and the harder it gets, the more of both your motives end up in view. What lands on you is not really their argument. It is their speed. Plain speech aimed at something you have held for a long time reads as an approach, whether or not they meant it that way, so your answers come back weightier than the occasion, and the silence before them can run long enough to become the answer. Neither of you has to announce a contest for one to be running. This one can sit under years of arrangements that nobody outside would call strained. Where it goes wrong is in the loop. A disagreement gets parked rather than finished, then reappears under a fresh heading three months later with both of you in the identical position. Nothing about the surface topic explains why it keeps coming back. What explains it is that giving way here feels to you like conceding something much larger than the point in front of you, and that reading is not wrong, which is exactly why the loop is so durable. The traction is equally real. Depth does not get tested by agreement. Effort of a certain size only happens against resistance, and this person will not go along with you to keep the peace. What you build in reaction to them tends to hold up in a way your uncontested work does not, and you may notice that some of your best years of output sit inside the range of a connection you would not describe as comfortable. None of this describes conduct. The angle supplies friction. What anybody makes of friction belongs to that person and not to a chart. Where you develop is in learning what the holding costs you. Outlasting people works, it has worked for a long time, and it quietly spends years on a contest nobody else agreed to score. This is the connection that makes the price visible, because the person across from you does not tire and does not go away. Saying the want plainly, in ordinary words, with no case built around it, is the move that ends the loop, and it is the move your equipment is least inclined to make.

Your weight does not slow them down, and that single fact changes more than it should. Most people meet your intensity by adjusting to it: they get careful, or they go quiet, or they take on a managing tone. Their Mars skips all of it. It takes what you bring and turns it into something to do, usually within the day, and the speed of the conversion is what you notice first. What flows out of you is a reason worth the effort. Drive with no serious object burns fast and leaves a person wondering why they bothered. You give theirs a subject with a floor under it. Around you they take on longer, harder, less popular work than they otherwise would, and they stay with it past the point where interest usually runs out, because you have made the object matter and it goes on mattering. What flows back is discharge. Depth held in with no outlet turns around and starts working on old material. Their willingness to act gives yours a route into the world, and the relief of that is close to physical. Near them you brood less and finish more. Neither of you breaks easily in an argument. The temperature can climb without the connection feeling at risk, which is uncommon enough that people with this contact tend to measure other company against it and find that other company flinches. Smooth angles include no resistance, and that is where the real exposure sits. Escalation does not feel like escalation here. It feels like agreement. A shared decision to lean harder on a situation can carry the two of you well past what either would have done alone, with nothing in the geometry to mark the line as you go over it. The quieter waste is simpler. The channel is open, it asks nothing, and a whole acquaintance can pass in good company with the serious capacity never once put to work. You develop here by choosing the target rather than letting it choose itself. Your instinct is to wait until something becomes unavoidable and then commit everything you have. Their instinct is to start. Borrowing a little of that, and spending it on something you picked rather than something that came looking for you, is the most useful thing this contact has to hand you.

They begin things. You are the one who will not let a thing be dropped, and the two of you stand at opposite ends of that. Your Pluto opposes their Mars, so everything they start arrives in front of your capacity to intensify, and everything you carry sits in permanent view of somebody whose answer to a problem is to move on it now. An opposition sets the stakes without consulting anyone. They raise something ordinary. It comes back from you with more behind it than the occasion contained. They want a decision by Friday, and you work on a timescale where Friday is not a real unit. No conversation is going to reconcile those two clocks. It is the shape of the angle, and it stays for the duration. What they meet in you is something they cannot outrun, and outrunning is their usual solution. They push, and the far side of the push has more mass in it than they planned for. What you meet in them is a person who will not wait for you to be ready, whose willingness to act while the outcome is undecided looks careless to you right up to the point where it works. Each of you can quietly hand the other a quality you would rather not own. You give them the whole appetite for a fight and keep the position of being merely thorough. They give you the whole weight of the thing and treat their own stakes as ordinary preference. While that exchange is running, whatever the two of you actually disagree about never reaches the table, and it can wait there for years. An opposition completes as well as confronts, and both halves here are real. What you have is staying power: you can remain with a difficult thing long after it stops being interesting, and you can see the bottom of a situation. What they have is the nerve to move without knowing. Neither capacity transfers by admiration. Living across from it in a person you cannot dismiss is the closest thing to instruction on offer, and the instruction is slow. Put to work, the two of you cover ground neither covers alone, though the division is rarely negotiated out loud. They take the first step and absorb the early failures. You are still there in the third year, when the thing either becomes real or does not. Between those two points sit most of your arguments and most of the accuracy. What turns a standoff into something workable is your willingness to let their speed count as an answer rather than an evasion, and to own your own weight instead of presenting it as patience. You stay opposite. That was never going to resolve. What it can hand you, over a long acquaintance, is the experience of acting before you are certain, which is the one thing your own equipment will not teach you.

Their optimism does not stay decorative around you. Your Pluto has joined their Jupiter, the part of them that decides what is possible, what may be promised, and how large a plan gets before anybody checks it. Fused with your depth, a loose opinion of theirs picks up a foundation, and a passing enthusiasm turns into a program with dates and money attached. They may not be able to say when that happened. The pressure you put on their faith is the interesting half. You are not a skeptic exactly. You take what they believe more seriously than they do, which is a different and harder thing to be on the receiving end of. When they say something could be done, you want to know who would be exposed by doing it and what would be left standing afterwards. Most people let a large statement go by. You follow it to the bottom, and their beliefs come back from that trip either much sturdier or gone. What comes to you is scale, and it may be what you were shortest on. Your kind of intensity runs narrow. It goes a long way down on a few subjects, often ones with a private history attached, and it can spend a whole life there. Their Jupiter keeps proposing a wider field: further off, less personal, larger than the thing you have been holding. In their company you take on ambitions you would have called grandiose in anybody else's mouth. There is permission in it too, and that is no small transfer at this end of a chart. Depth like yours tends to be rationed. It gets held in reserve, spent carefully, kept out of sight by an old conviction that appetite on this scale needs justifying. Their belief does not share the conviction, and the disagreement gets settled by example rather than by argument. What you had been keeping to yourself starts to look like a plan, and that door does not shut again easily. Excess is the standing hazard and it should be said plainly. Nothing in this contact contains a limit. Depth carrying that much conviction can turn a reasonable project into a campaign, and a fair opinion into a position that no longer hears an objection. Neither of you is the one who says that is enough, so the limit has to be imported, from outside company or from a habit of asking that you keep on purpose. Onlookers tend to register the size of what the two of you take on before either of you does, and they begin addressing you as a single position. A chart can show how much force is in play. It cannot show what anybody decides to do with it. What changes in you is what you will admit to wanting. Your equipment is built to keep things covered. Beside a person of that much conviction the covering stops being automatic, and you find you can state an ambition in daylight without feeling that you have handed somebody a weapon.

Most people never find this one. Your Pluto and their Jupiter reach each other at a workable angle: your depth is available to their sense of scale, their scale is available to your depth, and nothing in the geometry picks the connection up on your behalf. Used, it works like this. They open a situation out: how far it could go, and why the limit everybody accepts is only a habit. You come back with where the weight sits. Who controls the piece that matters, what it will cost to keep, which part of the plan is doing all the work. The unusual thing is that none of this flattens them. Jupiter at this angle takes the correction as information and keeps the ambition, which is not the response you normally get when you tell somebody what a thing will actually require. Your side of the trade is range, and it is worth more to you than you may register. Your attention is concentrated by nature. It goes a long way down on a few subjects and does not travel sideways easily. They keep opening the frame: another field, another scale, the same force spent on something further from home. Around them you take on work you would have dismissed as unserious, with your thoroughness still attached. There is a conversational use as well. Ambition, leverage, and what you would do with more of either can be discussed here at face value, without anybody treating the subject as a confession. Conversations of that kind are uncommon, and they tend to enlarge what a person believes they are allowed to want. The limit is the same as the offer. No pressure attaches to this angle. You can go years enjoying their company, half aware that the two of you could take on something substantial, and never do it, because the light version is always available and nothing complains. It gets built on purpose or not at all. The move is to put the guarded thing in front of them rather than the version you are comfortable discussing, and to let a wider read stand where it contradicts your own. A few rounds of that and your depth stops being private property and starts working on something with room in it, which is the trade this angle was built for and the one it will never require.

You know what things cost. They believe the door is open. Those two convictions grind against each other here, and not occasionally: it shows in how a plan gets discussed, in what either of you calls a fair offer, in the gap between what is possible and what is actually available. They are likely to feel you as a chill on their enthusiasm, and in fairness you often are. They name a possibility. Most company answers with agreeable noise. What they get from you is a pause, or a question about the part they waved past, or nothing at all, which reads as a verdict. Sometimes it is a verdict. Sometimes it is only you working, since your sort of answer takes its time to surface. Either way they stop, and Jupiter has no graceful way of stopping. What their ease does to you is the half that rarely gets written down, and it is where this angle bites. Their generosity is real, unmeasured, and handed over without a ledger, and it presses on a conviction of yours that every open door has a price on it and somebody is already paying. You may find you cannot accept an offer that has nothing behind it. That reflex kept you safe for a long time. It is not always right, and this is the connection where the difference gets tested. Permission is the recurring subject even when neither of you names it. Their position is that more ought to be available than currently is. Yours is that availability is granted by someone, for reasons, and the reasons are usually visible if you look. So an argument that began about a schedule or a sum ends up about authority, and the two of you can spend a whole evening on the surface topic without either of you mentioning the real one. Popular writing on this pair leans hard on the word power, so a flat statement belongs here. A square puts force between what you intensify and what they enlarge. Force in a chart is not conduct in a life, and no aspect has ever described how a person treats anybody. None of that friction is wasted, and none of it feels good while it is happening. Your depth gets pushed on by someone who refuses to accept that the ceiling is fixed, and beliefs of yours that were formed once and never revisited do not survive much of that. Your sense of what is available can widen while your accuracy holds, and that combination is not one you can arrange on your own. What changes the loop, when the same disagreement has come back under a new heading for the third time, is candor about the wanting. Say plainly that you want something, instead of proving that the alternative is unaffordable, and they can meet you on it. Analysis is very hard to argue with, and being hard to argue with is how a disagreement lasts a decade.

They find you easy to believe in, and you find their optimism unusually hard to dismiss. Your Pluto trines their Jupiter, so depth and scale move between you with nothing in the way. What you take seriously they are prepared to think large about, and the handover happens before either of you has argued for it. The first thing you notice is that your weight is not treated as a problem. Most company meets the full size of your interest in something with caution, or with a joke, or by changing the subject. They meet it with room. They take the thing you are serious about and ask what it could become, and the asking is genuine rather than polite. For a person accustomed to being the heaviest presence in the conversation, that is a new experience of your own equipment. You put a floor under them. Belief is what Jupiter is good at; the last mile is not. It opens, promises, and moves on before the promise has been kept. Around you their large intentions pick up follow-through, cost estimates, and a reason to still be at work in the third year once the excitement has gone. You may never learn how much of that they credit to you, since they will experience it as their own resolve. The obvious risk in a smooth angle is that nothing here says enough. Together the two of you can go considerably further than either would alone, and at every step it will feel like the reasonable next move. Escalation with no resistance in it does not register as escalation. Money, standing, and influence are the usual arenas, because this pairing tends to be effective around all three and comfortable while it is. The quieter risk is borrowed judgment. It is easy to let their sense of scale decide what is worth doing while you supply only the depth, and to find yourself committed at a size you never independently chose. The same borrowing happens in reverse, with your seriousness standing in for a check they never made. Then there is simple waste. Trines require nothing of anybody. Years can pass in which the fit is obvious, the conversation is good, and no weight is ever placed on the connection, and the pleasantness disguises the fact that nothing is happening. What this offers, worked rather than admired, is uncommon. Somebody who meets the size of what you carry, does not ask you to carry less of it, and thinks it should be aimed at something larger than your own history is not a person you meet often. What it costs is vigilance of a kind neither body supplies. Depth does not doubt itself and faith does not either, so a second look at what the two of you are doing has to be arranged on purpose.

Everything you would rather examine in private sits across from a person who thinks most things should be out in the open and larger than they are. Your Pluto opposes their Jupiter, and neither view collapses into the other, so both stay in the room for the duration. Their instinct is to widen. Yours is to go down. Meeting a difficulty, they look for more space around it, another option, a bigger frame in which the trouble is smaller. Meeting the same difficulty, you look for what is underneath it. Both methods work. Neither of you can perform the other's, and each of you can see exactly what the other's leaves out. You are likely to experience them as somebody you cannot get to be serious, which is not quite fair to them. What they refuse is not gravity. It is your assumption that the darker reading is the true one. They keep suggesting that a question you closed years ago, at cost, is less closed than you think, and that the limit you can describe in detail was put there by somebody and can be moved. Depending on the day, that is either a relief or an intrusion. From their side you are the one who cannot be cheered. Encouragement is their standard instrument and it does not work on you. Where most people take the wider picture and feel lighter, you want to know what the width is concealing, and often enough you find something, which makes the habit very hard to give up. Say the word power and neither of you would claim it, and it is the axis this runs on anyway. The recurring question is whose estimate governs. Was the last offer a gift or a position? Whose account of the cost is the one everybody works from? In a shared undertaking this shows up as arguments about how big to go that are never really about the number. In closer company it becomes a slow negotiation over which of you may say a want out loud without dressing it as something else. Both of you have something you would rather see in the other person. It suits you to treat them as the credulous one and yourself as merely accurate. It suits them to treat you as the calculating one and skip their own appetite. While that arrangement holds, each of you is arguing with a piece of your own equipment. The completing half of this is not a consolation prize. Your depth has no instinct for room, and their reach has no instinct for consequence. Facing them across a table teaches you what no agreeable company could, which is that opening a thing up is not the same as losing it. Whatever the two of you become to each other, the thing likely to stay with you is a larger sense of what is genuinely available, reached without surrendering anything you know about what things cost.
